deep.reconstruction:
This page is printed text from an 18th-century German arithmetic textbook (Leiste's Arithmetik, p. 53, signature D3). It continues a section on the rule of three (Regel de tri). The left-margin strip of handwriting is bleed-through or the edge of the facing manuscript page: the √2 convergents 47321/33461 and factorizations such as 27.73 and 197.199 belong to the previous page. The page contains no Gauss-specific mathematics.

The author's point: so-called 'inverse' rule-of-three problems do not need the terms of the proportion swapped. Treat the whole quantity as 1 and divide it by the given terms. Each term then enters as a unit fraction 1/a, and 1/a : 1/b = b : a (§128).

(1) Carpenters. 4 carpenters finish the house in 8 weeks; how long do 6 take?
- Work = 1, so 1/4 : 1/6 = 6/24 : 4/24 = 6 : 4 = 8 : x.
- Hence x = 4·8/6 = 16/3 weeks = 5 1/3 weeks.
- The book writes this as 5 weeks 2 days, which assumes a 6-day working week (my inference).

(2) Provisions. Provisions feed 500 soldiers for 6 months; how many must leave so they last 10 months?
- 1/6 : 1/10 = 10 : 6 = 500 : 300.
- So 300 men can be fed for 10 months, and 200 must leave.

(3) Bread weight (assize of bread). The Berlin Scheffel of wheat costs 1 Reichsthaler and is charged to the baker at 1 rthl 14 ggr.
- With 1 rthl = 24 ggr, that is 38 ggr. A 3-pfennig roll then weighs 12½ Lot.
- When the Scheffel costs 2 rthl, charged at 2 rthl 17 ggr = 65 ggr, the roll must weigh x.
- 1/38 : 1/65 = 65 : 38 = 12.5 : x, so x = 12.5·38/65 = 2.5·38/13 = 95/13 = 7 4/13 Lot.

(4) Measures (posed here, solved on p. 54). Two measures B and A are in ratio 3 : 2, and length C = 4 B. Find C in units of A.
- The answer on the next page is C/3 : C/2 = 2 : 3 = 4 : x, so x = 6.
- The catchword 'C/3 :' at the foot of the page anticipates that line.
errors: '5 Wochen 2 Tage' is 5 1/3 weeks only under a 6-day (working) week; with a 7-day week 1/3 week is 2 1/3 days. This is a convention, not a slip.

results.what: Inverse proportion handled as a direct proportion of unit fractions (1/a : 1/b = b : a), applied to work-time, provisions-consumers and price-weight problems
results.modern_name: Inverse proportion / inverse rule of three

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a printed elementary arithmetic textbook page, not Gauss's own mathematics. The handwritten numbers at the left edge belong to the facing manuscript page (√2 convergents), not to this page.

checkable.asserts: provisions for 500 men over 6 months last 300 men 10 months; 200 must leave
1 rthl 14 ggr = 38 ggr and 2 rthl 17 ggr = 65 ggr (24 ggr per rthl)
4 units of the larger measure B equal 6 units of A when B:A = 3:2

transcription_corrections: The handwritten fragments visible in the far-left margin (79., 47321, 33461 p, 13, 27.73, 97.199, 27.27.73.73..., 1321, 100625, 750625, 99, 07, 243419299, 347741856, etc.) are the edge of the facing manuscript page, not part of p. 53.
The footer 'D 3' is the printer's signature mark. 'C:' with '3' below is the catchword 'C/3 :' (fraction), continuing on p. 54.
'§. 128.' and '§. 9.' are cross-references within the textbook; the transcription is otherwise accurate.
